correctness.rationale: After a common sign change and permutation the centered vector is (a,b,-c), c=a+b>0 and a≥b≥0. Convolving the two positive exponentials with the negative one yields the displayed positive-side divided difference and the negative-side exponential with coefficient c/((a+c)(b+c)). Differentiating u exp(-t/u)/(u+c) at fixed c converts the divided difference into a positive integral; integrating t^s gives the two powers of u with precisely the coefficients in (1) after division by Γ(s+1). The b=0 endpoint is integrable (the term u^{s+1} stays integrable with up to two logarithmic derivatives), and a=b uses the single derivative at a. Gamma duplication gives the claimed ratio. The two kernel curvatures are bounded below by 1/(2(s+2)) and 1/(2(s+2))−1/(s+1)^2, respectively, both positive at every s≥2. Differentiation of the positive mixture gives an average curvature plus the variance of its log-derivatives, so strictness holds on the full interval. For variance-normalized Y, Theorem 1 of arXiv:2602.03058v1, equation (6), applies at all real orders ≥2 and gives h(s)≥h(2)=0. Thus s h′(s)−h(s) starts nonnegative and strictly increases for s>2, giving strict growth of the norm ratio including comparisons with p=2. Replay: see RESULT.md, Steps 1–4, and the inspected verification/check_moments.py for optional finite diagnostics; its logged count is not an independent run or a continuum certificate.
